articles.title: Stop Syncing State With useEffect: 4 Bugs That Disappear When You Delete the Effect
articles.excerpt: Here is a pattern I see in almost every React codebase I read: const [fullName, setFullName] = useState(''); useEffect(() => { setFullName(firstName + ' ' + lastName); }, [firstName, lastName]); It wo…
articles.body: Here is a pattern I see in almost every React codebase I read: const [ fullName , setFullName ] = useState ( '' ); useEffect (() => { setFullName ( firstName + ' ' + lastName ); }, [ firstName , lastName ]); It works. It also renders twice every time a name changes, shows a stale value for one frame, and is a bug waiting to happen when someone adds a third dependency and forgets to list it. The fix is to delete the effect. Here are four cases where that is the right move. Why These Effects Cause Bugs An effect runs after React has painted the screen. So any state you set inside it means: React renders with the old value and paints it. The effect runs and calls setState . React renders again with the new value. The user can see step 1. That is the flicker.

articles.title: How to set your freelance hourly rate: a formula you can check against your own numbers
articles.excerpt: Most freelancers set their rate by looking at what others charge. That tells you what the market tolerates, not whether the rate keeps you in business. A better start is a floor: the lowest rate at wh…
articles.body: Most freelancers set their rate by looking at what others charge. That tells you what the market tolerates, not whether the rate keeps you in business. A better start is a floor: the lowest rate at which you still earn what you need. Here is the formula and a worked example. The formula Minimum hourly rate = (target net income + business costs + taxes) / billable hours Each part is easy to underestimate. Target net income: what you want to take home in a year, after everything. Business costs: software, equipment, insurance, accounting, coworking, training. Add them up for a full year. Taxes and social contributions: as self-employed you pay them yourself, so include them in the total you need to cover. Billable hours: not 40 per week.

articles.title: PRD vs BRD vs SRS: Which Requirements Document Do You Need?
articles.excerpt: A BRD (business requirements document) explains why a project exists and what the business needs from it. A PRD (product requirements document) describes what the product does for its users. An SRS (s…
articles.body: A BRD (business requirements document) explains why a project exists and what the business needs from it. A PRD (product requirements document) describes what the product does for its users. An SRS (software requirements specification) states, precisely enough to build and test against, how the system must behave. Most small projects need the content of all three but not three separate files. The three documents in one table The names are used loosely, and two companies can mean slightly different things by "PRD". The table shows the most common reading of each. BRD PRD SRS Question it answers Why are we doing this, and what must the business get? What will the product do, for whom? Exactly how must the system behave?

articles.body: You write in Markdown. Someone else wants a Word document. Usually that's fine, until the file has a table, an equation, or a code block, and the .docx you send comes out looking broken. This guide shows how to convert Markdown to Word properly, mostly with pandoc , and covers the problems I ran into after doing it a lot. The one-liner If you have pandoc installed, a basic Markdown to Word conversion is one command: pandoc notes.md -o notes.docx Headings become real Word heading styles (so the navigation pane and table of contents work), lists become real lists, and pipe tables become Word tables. articles.title: A 40-Line Python Script to Check hreflang Reciprocity on a Small Site
articles.excerpt: Multilingual sites usually break in a boring way. Someone adds a new language page, links it from the English version, and forgets that the new page must link back. Search engines treat hreflang annot…
articles.body: Multilingual sites usually break in a boring way. Someone adds a new language page, links it from the English version, and forgets that the new page must link back. Search engines treat hreflang annotations as valid only when they are reciprocal, so a missing return link quietly cancels the signal. You can catch most of these errors with a short script that fetches your pages and compares the annotations. This post walks through a minimal version you can adapt. What the script checks For every URL in a list, it will: Fetch the page and read all link rel="alternate" hreflang tags in the head. Record each language and the URL it points to. Fetch each alternate and confirm that it points back to the original with the correct language code.

articles.body: TL;DR Discord will begin making messages from eligible public servers available through Google and other search engines in mid-December. The change excludes private servers and DMs, but in many regions, eligible messages will be publicly searchable by default. Users and server admins can opt out before the rollout, but the controls currently require desktop or web access. Discord has become a treasure trove of useful information, but finding it through Google has often felt like a treasure hunt with no map. Companies like Samsung and Google, on the other hand, are still offering 5,000mAh to 6,000mAh batteries. New smartphone launches have become so common that it takes something special to really make a mark . There was a time when smartphone makers battled over who could pack the most megapixels into their phone’s camera. Now, we’re seeing something different: battery capacities. articles.body: Full spoilers follow for VisionQuest Episodes 5 & 6, which are streaming now on Disney+. articles.title: 5 Adult Fairy Tale Books That Are Magical From Start to Finish
articles.excerpt: Dive into fantastical worlds filled with wizards, fae, and dangerous quests
articles.body: Fairy tales are often the first stories kids learn from picture books, and the works of Hanna Diyab, the Brothers Grimm, and Hans Christian Andersen can help inspire a lifelong passion for reading. But just because you grow up, doesn’t mean you have to abandon the genre. Modern fantasy books often strive for epic scale and complex political scheming, but it can be just as satisfying to explore a wondrous world where brave heroes fall in love and find the courage to do what’s right. If you want to bring some more magic to your reading list, check out these five fairy tale novels for adults.

articles.title: How 'spacewalking' underwater made me feel like I was really in space
articles.excerpt: Analog Astronaut Commander and Aquanaut Michaela Musilova led underwater simulated “spacewalks” in low visibility to test astronaut safety and communication protocols during simulated space missions.
articles.body: I was breathing just fine through my life support systems, but I kept feeling an urge to double check that everything was ok with my "spacesuit" before heading out on this "spacewalk." I have worn many different types of spacesuits on Earth during my career, but for the first time in my life, I knew that I couldn’t just stop to breathe the air outside if there were an emergency. That's because I was underwater. On this excursion, I was leading a simulated space mission underwater called SEA STAR. My " spacesuit " was actually scuba diving gear, and the simulated spacewalks , or EVAs (Extra-Vehicular Activities), included outings where we explored underwater environments.

articles.title: NASA Invites Media to Crew Completion of Yearlong Mars Simulation
articles.excerpt: The four volunteers who lived and worked in a simulated NASA Mars mission for more than a year will exit their habitat on Saturday, Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation in a facility at the agency’s J…
articles.body: Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) Mission 2 crew members (from left) Ross Elder, Matthew Montgomery, Ellen Ellis, and James Spicer, pose for a photo on Oct. 8, 2025. Credit: NASA The four volunteers who lived and worked in a simulated NASA Mars mission for more than a year will exit their habitat on Saturday, Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation in a facility at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Health and performance data collected from the simulation can help NASA develop methods to counter human spaceflight risks for future Artemis and Moon Base missions. Beginning at 3 p.m. EDT, NASA will provide live coverage of the volunteers’ departure from the Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA, pronounced cha-pea’-ah) mission habitat.
